SolarEdge — product lines and unit economics

SEDG-unit-econ-2026-10-14 · USD · series 2026-10-15T04:00:00Z · built 2026-10-15 04:15 UTC

Dig question: Is SolarEdge growing beyond home rooftops into commercial and utility-scale solar, in volume and in revenue, at prices that hold up?

Through the quarter ended June 30, 2026.

The short answer from the filings: commercial, yes; utility-scale, no. Commercial products went from about a third of the megawatts SolarEdge ships to around two thirds in 2023–2024. Utility-scale never shows up as its own line. The large-format bets that would have pointed that way (Kokam storage systems, e-Mobility and the tracker business) are all shut. Commercial watts also sell for less, so a shift in mix grows megawatts faster than dollars.

SolarEdge prints revenue by product, but never by customer type. So the mix below is the share of megawatts shipped that management states on the calls. For 2018–2024 those figures come from third-party call transcripts (stockanalysis.com, roic.ai), not from filings or SolarEdge's own documents. Every split it does not print is left blank.

What it sells

Every line outside solar inverters, optimizers and home batteries has been closed or sold. Critical Power was discontinued in June 2022, and the e-Mobility vehicle business in October 2023. Energy storage in South Korea followed in November 2024, and Automation Machines was sold in 2024. The 2025 10-K says: "We have discontinued our e-Mobility business, energy storage business, and PV Tracker business" (10-K for 2025, Feb 25, 2026).

Volume and mix

The commercial share passed half in Q2 2020 and stayed at or above 60% from Q2 2023 to Q4 2024. That happened while total megawatts fell from 4.3 GW to under 1 GW a quarter. It dropped back to 50% in Q1 2025, the last quarter SolarEdge gave it. Management describes C&I as a rooftop business: "more than 50% of U.S. C&I rooftop installations in the most recent report" (Q2 2026 prepared remarks, Aug 5, 2026). At the 2026 investor day it said: "In C&I, we are winning" (Sep 10, 2026).

Price and profit

The 10-Ks tie the mix to price year after year. The 2024 10-K blames part of the price decline on "an increase in the sale of commercial products that are characterized by lower ASP per watt" (10-K for 2024, Feb 25, 2025). The stated solar price fell from 26.9 cents a watt in Q1 2022 to 17.3 cents in Q1 2025 ("ASP per Watt, was 17.3 cents", Q1 2025 prepared remarks, May 6, 2025). Battery prices fell from $475 per kWh in Q3 2023 to $403 in Q4 2023, and to $262 for PV-attached batteries by Q4 2024 (call transcripts). Solar revenue per watt shipped (derived) mostly sits between $0.20 and $0.29. So more commercial volume needs more megawatts for each dollar.

Where it sells

Europe was 64% of revenue in 2023 and 27% in 2025. In Q2 2026, SolarEdge said it "more than doubled our revenue year-over-year" in Europe, and named storage demand ahead of the end of net metering as a driver (Q2 2026 prepared remarks).

Bridge to valuation

The key-metrics page carries revenue, free cash flow and the multiple. This page shows what sits underneath them: a rooftop business that is shifting toward commercial roofs and Europe, with no printed utility-scale line. Management runs 2026 on four priorities: "driving profitable growth, expanding global market share, scaling the SolarEdge Nexis platform, and advancing our opportunity in power infrastructure for the AI factories of the future" (Q2 2026 prepared remarks, Aug 5, 2026). On Nexis, it said it began rolling out the three-phase version in Europe "with shipments exceeding 60 million Dollars" in Q2 2026 (same document). The next growth leg management names is power for AI data centres, with "pilot installations in 2027 and volume shipments in 2028" (Q2 2026 prepared remarks). There is no revenue from it yet.

Open gaps

  • Revenue by customer type (residential, commercial, utility): never printed. The only split is the share of megawatts shipped, stated on calls.
  • Utility-scale: no product line, revenue or shipment figure. Utility appears only inside a combined commercial-and-utility share, Q3 2024 to Q1 2025.
  • Price per watt and per watt-hour: levels are stated only on calls and remarks, Q3 2021 to Q1 2025, and not in filings. Solar is missing for Q3 2022, Q3 2023 and Q1 2024. Nothing is stated after Q1 2025, and the 10-K yearly change is blank for 2025.
  • Shipments: replaced by units recognized as revenue from Q4 2025; Q2 2026 printed neither.
  • Segments: one reportable segment from 2025. Segment gross profit for 2024 is not printed in the old form.
  • Home battery revenue before 2021 and storage systems before 2022: inside Others until later 10-Ks broke them out.
  • Critical power and automation machines: never broken out.
  • Commercial share: not stated for Q4 2018, Q3–Q4 2019 and Q4 2020. The Q1 2023 transcript gives 68% commercial and 42% residential, which do not add up. Neither the Q1 2023 slides (2.1 GW of commercial inverters, no share) nor roic.ai confirms a figure.

Sources

  • SolarEdge 10-K filings, fiscal 2015 to 2025 (SEC EDGAR, 14 documents): product, segment, regional revenue, and yearly price changes.
  • SolarEdge quarterly results press releases, 2015 to 2026 (93 documents): shipments, solar segment revenue and margin.
  • SolarEdge earnings-call prepared remarks, Q1 2025 to Q2 2026 (6 documents): the Q1 2025 commercial-and-utility share, the Q1 2025 price levels, priorities and Nexis.
  • SolarEdge earnings slides and supplemental information (81 documents): checks only.
  • Third-party call transcripts, not SolarEdge documents: stockanalysis.com (Q1 2018 to Q2 2026 and the 2026 investor day) and roic.ai (fiscal 2016 to 2017). These are the source of the commercial share for 2018–2024 and of the price levels for Q3 2021–Q4 2024.
